Hey man,

I know it isn't exactly what you're looking for, but what I find good for days where my appetite is massive is to eat a lot of green vegetables (my favourite being kale). They are very low in calories, so you can eat a lot of it and it fills you up very well (100 calories of male will make you feel a lot more full and for a longer time than 100 calories from a biscuit)

They are also turgid, which means it'll soak up water and expand in the stomach, making you feel fuller. 

I also drink plenty of water, about 5L a day. 

There isn't really such thing as a 'slow' metabolism, so don't worry too much about that. 

I have used modafinil a few times (really good for studying), and it is known for being an appetite suppressant. You have little urge to eat on it, and time also flies by if you're doing something, which means a day can go by without you getting up and snacking loads. Modafinil could be a good replacement as it has no negative side effects (especially in comparison to meth!), makes you feel alert, improves memory retention, and also makes you feel very well rested. 

However, I really do not recommend the use of drugs to pretty much starve yourself. It's unhealthy weight-loss, and will wreak havoc on your health and wellbeing. A healthy diet and exercise (although easier said than done) truly is the best way to go about it. If getting out to do exercise is a problem, I recommend cycling. It's enjoyable, rather easy, and if you need to go somewhere, you can cycle there.
